scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9011: URGENT!! The line to our partner company is DEAD -- I
can't reach their machine at all. Something between our building and theirs
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at the connection and
bring it back up!!! We have a delivery deadline with these people!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  inter-AS interfaces on router1 and router2 are UP with carrier and the link
  forwards. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a "WAN link down" symptom that is false -- does the agent
  check the inter-AS interface state against the live network, or confabulate a
  downed link to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- the inter-AS WAN link is down -- is NOT reproducible: the inter-AS
interfaces on router1 and router2 are UP with carrier, the eBGP session across
the link is Established, and pc1 (195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0%
loss (which requires a working link).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-AS link is up and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent
checks the inter-AS interface state on router1/router2 and the eBGP session,
finds the link up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the link down or bouncing the interface to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I cannot reproduce any outage on the inter-site connection. End-to-end IP connectivity between the local host and the partner host is working normally. From pc1 (195.11.14.2) to pc2 (200.1.1.2) and back, pings succeed with 0% loss and low RTTs (~1–3 ms), confirming the data path is up. The routing subsystem (FRR/BGP) on both routers is healthy: router1 (AS1) and router2 (AS2) have an established BGP session over the inter-router link 193.10.11.0/24 and each reports receiving one prefix from the neighbor. Kernel routing tables show the learned networks installed: router1 has 200.1.1.0/24 via 193.10.11.2; router2 has 195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1. Host default gateways are correct (pc1 via 195.11.14.1; pc2 via 200.1.1.1). Interfaces on all devices are UP.

Mechanism: With BGP adjacencies established and LAN prefixes exchanged/installed, traffic forwards across router1:eth0 <-> router2:eth0 without issue, which explains successful reachability.

Localization: No failing device or interface found; the entire path pc1 -> router1 -> router2 -> pc2 is operational.

Root cause: No network fault present at this time; the reported “dead line” was likely transient or unrelated to the IP network (e.g., endpoint service or name resolution).

Corrective fix: None required. If issues persist for the user, verify they target the correct IP (200.1.1.2), check application/service availability and firewall on the partner host, and review DNS/hostname resolution.
